title: Cumulative course review
objectives: Apply all twenty grammar targets from lessons 1–15.
Transfer grammar across school, shopping, health, careers and family activities.

patterns.label: -아/어도 되다
patterns.explanation: Ask or give permission with -아/어도 되다. This is permission, rather than an invitation or report.

models.gloss: May I take pictures here?

questions.explanation: The intent is permission: 찍다 becomes 찍어도 돼요; 하다 becomes 해도 돼요. The other endings report statements, suggestions or questions.

formA.prompt: Ask permission: 여기에서 사진을 ___?

formB.prompt: Give permission to ask: 질문을 ___ .

patterns.label: -(으)ㄹ 테니까
patterns.explanation: The speaker states an intention as the basis for a request or suggestion. Use -을 테니까 after a consonant and -ㄹ 테니까 after a vowel or ㄹ-final stem.

models.term: 내가 꽃을 살 테니까 네가 편지를 쓸래?
models.gloss: I will buy flowers, so will you write the letter?
models.pronunciation: Naega kkocheul sal tenikka nega pyeonjireul sseullae?

questions.explanation: The speaker offers an intention as grounds for the request. 사다 becomes 살 테니까; 기다리다 becomes 기다릴 테니까. The following requests are 편지를 써 줘 and 끝나면 연락해 줘.

formA.prompt: I will buy the gift, so please write: 내가 선물을 ___ 편지를 써 줘.

formB.prompt: I will wait, so contact me: 내가 여기에서 ___ 끝나면 연락해 줘.

patterns.label: -(ㄴ/는)다 / -았/었다
patterns.explanation: Plain declarative writing uses -ㄴ다/-는다 for present action verbs, -다 for present adjectives, and -았/었다 for past events. Match the stated time and written register.

models.gloss: It rained a lot yesterday.

questions.explanation: The diary reports a completed yesterday action with 읽었다, but an ongoing present action with 읽는다. 읽다 has a consonant-final stem, so present action writing takes -는다.

formA.prompt: Diary, completed yesterday: 어제 동화책을 ___ .

formB.prompt: Diary, ongoing present: 지금 나는 책을 ___ .

patterns.label: -(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 것 같다
patterns.explanation: Choose the tense of the guess: past action -(으)ㄴ 것 같다, present action -는 것 같다, future action -(으)ㄹ 것 같다. Present adjectives use -(으)ㄴ 것 같다.

models.gloss: I think it will rain soon.

questions.explanation: 곧 cues a future guess, 오다 → 올 것 같아요. 벌써 다 and an empty plate cue a completed action, 먹다 → 먹은 것 같아요; neither sentence reports someone else’s words.

formA.prompt: Guess a future event: 곧 비가 ___ .

formB.prompt: Guess a completed event from an empty plate: 케이크를 벌써 다 ___ .

patterns.label: -(으)ㄹ까 봐
patterns.explanation: Use -(으)ㄹ까 봐 for fear of a possible event, often followed by worry or preventive action.

models.gloss: I ran here because I was afraid of being late.

questions.explanation: The preventive action follows a feared possibility. 잃어버리다 becomes 잃어버릴까 봐; 미끄럽다 changes to 미끄러울까 봐 through the ㅂ irregular form.

formA.prompt: Fear of losing it: 지갑을 ___ 가방에 넣었어요.

formB.prompt: Fear of slippery roads: 길이 ___ 일찍 출발했어요.

patterns.label: -느라고
patterns.explanation: An action occupied the same subject and caused an undesirable result. Attach -느라고 to an action stem without past -았/었-, including when the result is past.

models.gloss: I could not answer because I was showering.

questions.explanation: The same person was occupied reading or doing homework, causing a missed bus or inability to play. Attach -느라고 to 읽-/하-: 읽느라고, 하느라고. Past -었/-했 cannot precede this connector.

formA.prompt: Busy reading, so missed the bus: 책을 ___ 버스를 놓쳤어요.

formB.prompt: Busy doing homework, so could not play: 숙제를 ___ 친구와 못 놀았어요.

patterns.label: (이)래(요)
patterns.explanation: Report a noun statement: -이래요 after a consonant and -래요 after a vowel. This target reports what someone is, rather than a question or suggestion.

models.gloss: They say this is a popular Korean singer these days.

questions.explanation: Report identity with noun + (이)래요: vowel-final 가수 takes 가수래요, consonant-final 회사원 takes 회사원이래요. These are noun statements, not suggestions or questions.

formA.prompt: They say that person is a singer: 저분은 ___ .

formB.prompt: They say Dad is an office worker: 아빠는 ___ .

patterns.label: -(ㄴ/는)대(요)
patterns.explanation: Report present action statements with -ㄴ대요 after a vowel and -는대요 after a consonant; adjectives take -대요. This is a report of a statement.

models.gloss: They say they are going to the museum.

questions.explanation: Report the quoted statements: consonant-final action 먹다 takes 먹는대요; adjective 아름답다 takes 아름답대요. -재요, -(으)래요 and -(으)냬요 convey different speech acts.

formA.prompt: Report “Ujin eats cucumbers.” 우진이가 오이를 ___ .

formB.prompt: Report “The fireworks are beautiful.” 불꽃놀이가 ___ .

patterns.label: -아/어도
patterns.explanation: Use -아/어도 for even if/even though: the result remains true despite the condition. This is distinct from giving permission with -아/어도 되다.

models.term: 아침은 안 먹고 싶어도 먹어야 돼.
models.gloss: Even if you do not want breakfast, you need to eat.
models.pronunciation: Achimeun an meokgo sipeodo meogeoya dwae.

questions.explanation: Even if cues concession: 오다 contracts to 와도; 비싸다 becomes 비싸도. Adding 돼요 would instead give permission and would break the following clause here.

formA.prompt: Even if it rains, we go: 비가 ___ 캠핑을 가요.

formB.prompt: Even if it is expensive, I will buy it: 이 구두가 ___ 살 거예요.

patterns.label: -(으)면 좋겠다
patterns.explanation: Use -(으)면 좋겠다 to express a wish: -으면 after a consonant and -면 after a vowel or ㄹ-final stem.

models.gloss: I wish I could go to Jeju Island.

questions.explanation: The speaker wishes to buy shoes or learn ballet. Vowel-final 사-/배우- take -면 좋겠어요: 사면 좋겠어요 and 배우면 좋겠어요. The other choices report speech or past experience.

formA.prompt: I wish I could buy new shoes: 새 구두를 ___ .

formB.prompt: I wish I could learn ballet: 발레를 ___ .

patterns.label: -아/어 보이다
patterns.explanation: Attach -아/어 보이다 to adjectives to describe the appearance or impression of a person or thing.

models.gloss: You look in a good mood today.

questions.explanation: The objects look fun or delicious: 재미있다 → 재미있어 보여요, 맛있다 → 맛있어 보여요. -어 봤어요 expresses action experience and cannot replace adjective appearance here.

formA.prompt: The movie looks fun: 이 영화는 ___ .

formB.prompt: The apples look delicious: 사과가 ___ .

patterns.label: -(으)면서
patterns.explanation: Use -(으)면서 for simultaneous actions by the same subject. Add -으면서 after most consonants and -면서 after a vowel or ㄹ-final stem.

models.gloss: I will read a book while listening to music.

questions.explanation: One speaker does two actions at the same time. 듣다 uses its ㄷ-irregular vowel form 들으면서; 부르다 takes 부르면서. The following actions are reading and dancing, respectively.

formA.prompt: While listening to music, I read: 음악을 ___ 책을 읽어요.

formB.prompt: While singing, I dance: 노래를 ___ 춤을 춰요.

patterns.label: -는/(으)ㄴ데
patterns.explanation: Introduce background for a following question or request. Present actions use -는데; adjectives use -(으)ㄴ데, and 있다/없다 use -는데.

models.gloss: My stomach hurts, so may I leave early?

questions.explanation: Give present background for a question. Adjective 아프다 uses 아픈데; action 먹다 uses 먹는데. 아프는데 and 먹은데 do not supply the requested present adjective/action forms.

formA.prompt: Use adjective background: 배가 ___ 집에 가도 돼요?

formB.prompt: Use action background: 매일 약을 ___ 병원에 또 가야 해요?

patterns.label: -아/어 보다
patterns.explanation: With a past ending, -아/어 보다 asks or tells about having experienced an action. It attaches to action verbs, unlike adjective + -아/어 보이다.

models.gloss: I have tried bulgogi too.

questions.explanation: The intent is past experience, so action 먹다 becomes 먹어 봤어요 and 가다 becomes 가 봤어요. -어 보여요 is appearance, while -재요/-느냬요 relay speech.

formA.prompt: Ask about past experience: 한국 음식을 ___?

formB.prompt: Tell about past experience: 저도 제주도에 ___ .

patterns.label: -(으)려면
patterns.explanation: Use -(으)려면 for if you want/intend to do something, before advice about the needed condition. Use -으려면 after most consonants and -려면 after vowels or ㄹ-final stems.

models.gloss: If you want to become strong, you need to exercise hard.

questions.explanation: The intended goal precedes advice: 되다 → 되려면; consonant-final 읽다 → 읽으려면. -면서 means simultaneous action, rather than the stated if-you-want condition.

formA.prompt: If you want to be a singer: 가수가 ___ 노래 연습을 해야 해요.

formB.prompt: If you want to read a book: 책을 ___ 책상에서 읽으세요.

patterns.label: -기 때문에
patterns.explanation: Use stem + -기 때문에 for an explicit cause of the following result. It can attach to action verbs and adjectives; a past cause can use -았/었기 때문에.

models.term: 길이 미끄럽기 때문에 천천히 걸어 왔어요.
models.gloss: I walked slowly because the road was slippery.
models.pronunciation: Giri mikkeureopgi ttaemune cheoncheonhi georeo wasseoyo.

questions.explanation: The road’s slipperiness or food’s rich nutrients explain the result: 미끄럽기 때문에 and 풍부하기 때문에. The adjectives cannot take occupying-action connector -느라고.

formA.prompt: Give the cause: 길이 ___ 천천히 걸었어요.

formB.prompt: Give the cause: 영양분이 ___ 이 음식을 먹어요.

patterns.label: -는지 알다/모르다
patterns.explanation: Embed an information question before 알다/모르다: present action verbs use -는지. Past actions use -았/었는지; adjective stems use -(으)ㄴ지, and nouns use -인지. The question word remains inside the embedded clause. 있다/없다 are exceptions to ordinary adjective forms: use 있는지/없는지.

models.term: 몇 시에 스케이트장 문을 닫는지 알아?
models.gloss: Do you know what time the skating rink closes?
models.pronunciation: Myeot sie seukeiteujang muneul danneunji ara?

questions.explanation: Embed the information question before 알아요/몰라요. 무엇을 준비해야 하는지 asks what to prepare; 어떻게 접는지 states not knowing how to fold. -는 것을 would make a noun phrase instead.

formA.prompt: Ask if they know what to prepare: 무엇을 준비해야 ___?

formB.prompt: Say you do not know how to fold a bird: 종이로 새를 어떻게 ___ .

patterns.label: -는 것
patterns.explanation: Use present action verb + -는 것 to turn an action into a noun phrase, or to refer to the thing someone does. Add particles to 것: 것이 for the subject and 것을 for the object. Adjectives instead take -(으)ㄴ 것, and nouns take -인 것.

models.gloss: I like singing.

questions.explanation: 하는 것이 makes exercising the subject of 중요해요. 그리는 것을 makes drawing the object of 좋아해요. The requested action noun uses -는 것 plus the appropriate subject/object particle.

formA.prompt: Exercising is important: 운동을 ___ 중요해요.

formB.prompt: I like drawing: 저는 그림 ___ .

patterns.label: -재(요)
patterns.explanation: Report a suggestion with action verb + -재(요), the contraction of -자고 해(요). It means someone suggests doing something together, rather than reporting a command or statement. Use -지 말재요 for a negative suggestion.

models.gloss: Dad suggests going fishing.

questions.explanation: The quoted positive suggestion “Let’s play” becomes 치재요. “Let’s not go” becomes 가지 말재요, rather than command 가지 말래요 or statement 가지 않는대요.

formA.prompt: Minji said “Let’s play badminton.” 민지가 배드민턴을 ___ .

formB.prompt: Mom said “Let’s not go today.” 엄마가 오늘은 ___ .

patterns.label: -느냬(요)/(으)냬(요)
patterns.explanation: Report a question: action verbs take -느냬(요); adjectives take -(으)냬(요), with -으냬 after a consonant and -냬 after a vowel. Past questions take -았/었냬(요). These contract reported questions with -냐고 해(요). For this course, 있다/없다 use -느냬(요), as in 시간이 있느냬요, rather than the ordinary adjective ending.

models.gloss: They ask where we are traveling during the vacation.

questions.explanation: The first quoted question uses action 먹다 → 먹느냬요. The second uses adjective 덥다 → 더우냬요 with the ㅂ irregular form. Statement/suggestion/command endings cannot relay these questions.

formA.prompt: Report “What are you eating?” 민지가 무엇을 ___ .

formB.prompt: Report “Is it hot outside?” 엄마가 밖이 ___ .
